nodes.name: Schedule Trigger
nodes.notes: Safe dev interval (every 15 min). Calls LeadFlow's tick endpoint, which is itself idempotent and rate-limited, so a missed/overlapping run cannot double-send.

nodes.name: Manual Trigger
nodes.notes: Lets this workflow be executed immediately on demand for testing, without waiting for the schedule.

nodes.name: On-Demand Webhook
nodes.notes: Production webhook: POST http://localhost:5678/webhook/leadflow-outreach-tick — an external system (or this test) can invoke the exact same tick processing on demand, in addition to the schedule.

nodes.name: Call LeadFlow Tick
nodes.notes: LeadFlow owns all business logic here: which contacts are due, draft generation, quality checks, approval-gate enforcement, sending via the mock/real email provider, suppression checks, and idempotent message recording. This node only triggers that processing and reads back the result — no CRM logic lives in n8n. retryOnFail is intentionally left OFF so a transient failure is reported, not blindly retried into a duplicate send.

nodes.name: Log Success
nodes.notes: Logs a concrete, human-readable summary of what LeadFlow actually did this tick. Visible in the n8n execution log.

nodes.name: Log Failure
nodes.notes: Records the failure without retrying and without treating it as success. LeadFlow's own idempotency (per-draft idempotency_key on outreach_messages) means a later, healthy tick cannot double-send whatever this run failed to process.
